Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 21, verse 1:

Naming of the Surah

• It is called al-Anbiya' (The Prophets), because it contains a detailed account of sixteen of the prophets and messengers, what happened to them with their peoples, their calling of their peoples to the truth, and their patience with them.

Some of the Objectives of the Surah

• Warning against the Day of Reckoning and its nearness, mentioning some of its events and what precedes it, warning people against heedlessness of it, and affirming its occurrence by pointing to the all-encompassing knowledge of God over what is in the heavens and the earth.

• Pointing to the destruction of the deniers among earlier nations, the punishment that befell them, and the regret and remorse that overtook them when repentance and remorse no longer benefit. Within this is a warning to those who deny the Prophet ﷺ, and consolation to him (ﷺ) regarding their disbelief and denial.

• Demonstrating the unity of the message of the messengers: they all came calling to monotheism (tawhid) and the negation of association (shirk) in divinity, and refuting the claim of the polytheists that God has a son. It also shows that those whom they described thus, namely the angels, are only honoured servants who obey God, exalted is He.

• Establishing rational proofs against the falsity of multiple gods, and using cosmic signs to establish that God alone deserves divinity, oneness, and worship to the exclusion of others. It also hints that beyond this life there is another life, in which every soul will be recompensed for what it has earned, and it threatens those who do not believe in this by pointing to the annihilation of creation, and that no one among creation is eternal, and that they will all return to God.

• Mentioning the stories of the prophets and what their peoples did during their calling, and that the purpose of their stories is to affirm divinity, the messages, and resurrection. Within this is consolation to the Prophet (ﷺ) by mentioning their circumstances with their peoples, and affirmation that the Messenger (ﷺ) is only like his fellow messengers, and that he brought nothing but the like of what the messengers before him brought.

• Mentioning some of the portents of the Hour, namely the emergence of Gog and Magog (Ya'juj wa Ma'juj), the nearness of the Hour, the condition of the disbelievers and believers on the Day of the Great Terror, and the cosmic transformations that will occur on that day.

[Tafsir]

The time has drawn near for people to be reckoned for what they have put forward of deeds, yet the disbelievers live heedless of this reality, turning away from this warning.
Nothing of the Qur'an that is revealed and recited to them, renewing the reminder for them, is heard by them except as the hearing of play and mockery.

Their hearts are heedless of the Noble Qur'an, preoccupied with the falsehoods of this world and its desires, and they do not comprehend what it contains. Rather, the wrongdoers among the Quraysh secretly gathered together over a hidden matter: spreading what they would use to turn people away from believing in Muhammad (ﷺ), namely that he is a human being like them, differing from them in nothing, and that what he brought of the Qur'an is sorcery. "How then do you come to him and follow him, when you see that he is a human being like you?"

The Prophet ﷺ referred the matter to his Lord, glory be to Him, and said: ﴿My Lord knows every word in the heavens and the earth, and He knows what you conceal of your speech, and He is the All-Hearing of your utterances, the All-Knowing of your conditions.﴾ In this there is a warning and a threat to them.

Rather, the disbelievers denied the Qur'an. Some of them said: "It is a jumble of confused dreams with no reality to them." Others said: "It is a fabrication and a lie, and not a revelation." And others said: "Muhammad is a poet, and what he has brought is poetry. And if he wants us to believe him, let him bring us a tangible miracle, like the she-camel of Salih, the signs of Musa and Isa, and what the Messengers before him brought."

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 21, verse 6:

Not one town before them, of the disbelievers of Makkah, believed when the miracles they asked of their messenger came to them and were fulfilled; rather, they denied, so We destroyed them. Will the disbelievers of Makkah believe when the miracles they asked for are fulfilled? No indeed; they will not believe.

And We did not send before you, O Messenger, except men from among mankind to whom We revealed; We did not send angels. So ask, O disbelievers of Makkah, the people of knowledge of the earlier revealed Books, if you do not know this.

**Commentary of the King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on Surah 21, verse 8:**

We did not make those messengers who came before you to be beings beyond the nature of humans, not needing food or drink, nor were they immortal, never dying.

Commentary of the King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 21, verse 9:

Then We fulfilled for the prophets and their followers what We had promised them of victory and deliverance, and We destroyed those who transgressed against themselves through their disbelief in their Lord.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 21, verse 10:

We have sent down to you this Qur'an, in which is your honour and your nobility in this world and the Hereafter, if you remember by it. Will you not then understand what We have favoured you with over others?

And how many a town whose people were wrongdoers, in their disbelief in what their messengers brought them, did We destroy; so We destroyed them with a punishment that wiped them out entirely, and We brought into being after them another people.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 21, verse 12:

When these wrongdoers saw Our severe punishment descending upon them and witnessed its first signs, they suddenly began fleeing hastily from their town.

Then they were called out at that moment: "Do not flee, and return to your pleasures and luxury in your distracting worldly life and your well-built dwellings, perhaps you will be asked about something from your worldly life." This was said in a mocking and derisive manner toward them.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 21, verse 14:

So they had no answer except their acknowledgment of their sin and their saying: "Woe to us! Indeed we have wronged ourselves by our disbelief."

So that statement—that is, their calling down destruction upon themselves and their confession of wrongdoing—remained their plea, which they kept repeating, until We made them like a harvested field, extinguished, with no life left in them. So beware, you who are addressed, lest you persist in denying Muhammad (ﷺ), and there befall you what befell the nations before you.

Commentary of the King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 21, verse 16:

We did not create the heavens and the earth and what is between them in vain and without purpose, but to establish proof against you, O people, and so that you may reflect on all of that, and thereby know that the One who created these things has no likeness, and that worship is due to none but Him.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 21, verse 17:

Had We wished to take a pastime (lahw) of a son or a consort, We would have taken it from Our own presence, not from yours; We would not have done such a thing, since it is impossible that We should have a son or a consort.

This is the commentary (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on the verse, so the passage is a paraphrase of the Qur'anic verse itself. I'll translate it as it stands.

Rather, We hurl the truth against falsehood, and it crushes it, and behold, falsehood vanishes away. And woe to you, O polytheists, for the punishment in the Hereafter, because of your describing your Lord with attributes not befitting Him.

To Allah, glorified is He, belongs everyone in the heavens and the earth. Those who are with Him among the angels do not disdain to worship Him, nor do they tire of it. So how could it be permissible for others to be associated with Him, when they are His servants and His creation?
They glorify Allah and declare Him far above any imperfection constantly, never growing weary or tired.
How could the polytheists rightly take gods from the earth who are powerless and cannot bring the dead back to life?

If there were in the heavens and the earth gods other than Allah, the Glorified, managing their affairs, their order would have been disrupted. So exalted is Allah, Lord of the Throne, and sanctified above what the deniers and disbelievers attribute to Him, of falsehood, fabrication, and every deficiency.

The commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 21, verse 23:

Among the proofs of His being singular in creation and in worship is that He cannot be questioned about His decree concerning His creation, while all His creatures will be questioned about their deeds.

Have these polytheists taken gods besides Allah that benefit and harm, give life and cause death? Say, [O Messenger], to them: Bring your proof for what you have taken as gods. There is no evidence in the Qur'an that I have brought, nor in the earlier scriptures, for what you have gone off to believe. They associated partners with Allah only out of ignorance and blind imitation, and they turn away from the truth, denying it.
We did not send any messenger before you, O Messenger, except that We revealed to him that there is no deity worthy of worship except Allah. So devote your worship sincerely to Him alone.

The disbelievers said: "The Most Merciful has taken a son," claiming that the angels are the daughters of God. Far be God exalted above that. The angels are servants of God, honoured and brought near to Him, distinguished by virtues. In their excellent obedience they speak only what their Lord commands them, and they do no deed until He gives them permission.

The disbelievers said: "The Most Merciful has taken a son," claiming that the angels are the daughters of God. Far be God exalted above that. The angels are servants of God, honoured and brought near to Him, distinguished by virtues. In their excellent obedience they speak only what their Lord commands them, and they do no deed until He gives them permission.

None of the deeds of the angels, whether past or future, is hidden from Allah, the Glorified and Exalted. He knows them and records them against them. They do not intercede except for one whom Allah has approved for intercession, and they are fearful of Allah, cautious of opposing His command and His prohibition.
And whoever among the angels claims that he is a god besides Allah, (even) by way of supposition, his recompense is Hell. Thus do We recompense every wrongdoer who associates partners with Allah.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 21, verse 30:

Have those who disbelieved not known that the heavens and the earth were joined together, with no separation between them, so there was no rain from the sky and no plants from the earth? Then We separated them by Our power, sent down rain from the sky, brought forth plants from the earth, and made every living thing from water. Will these deniers not believe, so that they affirm what they witness and single out Allah alone for worship?

And We placed in the earth firm mountains so that it would not shake with its inhabitants, and We made in it wide roads, in hope that people would be guided to their livelihoods and to the oneness of their Creator.

And We made the sky a roof for the earth, with no pillar holding it up. It is protected and does not fall, and the devils cannot break through it. But the disbelievers are heedless of taking lessons from the signs of the sky (the sun, the moon, and the stars), unmindful and inattentive to reflecting on them.

God Almighty is the One who created the night so that people may rest in it, and the day so that they may seek their livelihood in it. He created the sun as a sign for the day, and the moon as a sign for the night. Each of them has an orbit in which it moves and glides, never deviating from it.

The Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 21, verse 34:

We did not grant any human being before you, O Messenger, permanence in this world. So if you die, will they hope to remain forever after you? That will not happen. In this verse there is evidence that al-Khidr (peace be upon him) has died, because he is a human being.

Every soul will taste death, without doubt, however long it may live in this world. Its existence in this life is only a trial, through the obligations of commands and prohibitions, and through the changing of circumstances, good and evil. Then its final return and destination after that is to God alone, for reckoning and recompense.

"When the disbelievers see you, O Messenger, they make gestures at you, mocking you, saying to one another: 'Is this the man who speaks ill of your gods?' And they deny the Most Merciful and His blessings, and what He has sent down of the Qur'an and guidance."

Man was created hasty; he rushes toward things and seeks their occurrence quickly. The Quraysh sought the punishment hastily and considered its coming slow, so Allah warned them that He would show them the punishment they were hastening for, so let them not ask Allah to hasten it and bring it sooner.
The disbelievers say, hastening the punishment and mocking: "When will what you promise us come to pass, O Muhammad, if you and those who follow you are truthful?"

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 21, verse 39:

If these disbelievers knew what they will face when they are unable to ward off the Fire from their faces and their backs, and they will have no helper to help them, they would not have persisted in their disbelief, nor would they have hastened their punishment.

And the Hour will surely come upon them suddenly, so they will be bewildered at that time and will fear with a great fear. They will be unable to ward off the punishment from themselves, and they will not be given respite to make up for (their failure to repent) with repentance or with an excuse.

This is a translation of the given passage. Note that the source sentence contains no Qur'anic quotation markers, so the verse paraphrase is translated as commentary text.

"And indeed, messengers before you, O Messenger, were mocked, so the punishment that had been the object of their mockery and ridicule befell those who used to mock them."

Say, [O Messenger], to these who hasten on the punishment: No one can protect you or guard you by night or by day, whether in your sleep or in your waking, from the punishment of the Most Merciful when it descends upon you. Rather, they are heedless and inattentive to the Qur'an and the admonitions of their Lord.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 21, verse 43:

Do they have gods that can protect them from Our punishment? Their gods cannot even help themselves, so how could they help those who worship them? And they cannot be given protection against Us.

The disbelievers and their forefathers were deceived by being granted respite, because of the wealth, sons and long lives they saw, so they persisted in their disbelief, never ceasing from it, and they thought they would not be punished, though they had neglected a established custom (of God). So God diminishes the land from its edges, by sending upon the polytheists the calamity that comes to them from every direction, and defeat. Could the disbelievers of Makkah escape the power of God, or avoid death?

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 21, verse 45:

Say, O Messenger, to those to whom you have been sent: "I only warn you of the punishment through revelation from Allah, which is the Qur'an. But the disbelievers do not listen to what is conveyed to them with the listening of contemplation when they are warned, so they gain no benefit from it."

This is the commentary on Surah 21 (al-Anbiya'), verse 46, from the Tafsir al-Muyassar (the "Simplified Tafsir," produced by the King Fahd Complex):

If even a portion of God's punishment were to touch the disbelievers, they would surely realize the consequence of their denial, and they would respond to it by calling down destruction upon themselves, because of their wronging of themselves through their worship of other than God.

God sets up the just scale for reckoning on the Day of Resurrection, and He will not wrong these or anyone else in the least. Even if an action is the weight of a mustard seed, whether good or evil, it will be counted in the account of its doer. And God suffices as the One who takes account of His servants' deeds and recompenses them for them.

We gave Musa and Harun a clear proof and a victory over their enemy, and the Scripture, which is the Tawrah (the Torah), by which We distinguished between truth and falsehood, and a light by which the God-fearing are guided, those who fear the punishment of their Lord. They are, from the Hour in which the Resurrection will occur, fearful and anxious.

We gave Musa and Harun a clear proof and a victory over their enemy, and the Scripture, which is the Tawrah (the Torah), by which We distinguished between truth and falsehood, and a light by which the God-fearing are guided, those who fear the punishment of their Lord. They are, from the Hour in which the Resurrection will occur, fearful and anxious.

This Qur'an that Allah sent down upon His Messenger Muhammad (ﷺ) is a reminder for whoever takes heed of it and acts upon its commands and avoids its prohibitions, abundant in good and great in benefit. Will you then deny it, when it is in the utmost clarity and manifestness?

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 21, verse 51:

"And We indeed gave Ibrahim (Abraham) his guidance before (the time of) Musa (Moses) and Harun (Aaron), and We were knowing of him, that he was worthy of it."
When he said to his father and his people: "What are these idols that you have fashioned, to which you remain devoted in worship?"
They said: "We found our fathers worshipping them, and we worship them in imitation of them."

**Commentary of the King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar, the "Simplified Exegesis") on Surah 21, verse 54:**

Ibrahim said to them: "You and your fathers have indeed been in clear and evident error, in your worship of these idols."
They said: "Is this message you have brought us true and serious, or is what you tell us the talk of a jester and mocker who does not know what he is saying?"

Ibrahim (peace be upon him) said to them: "Rather, your Lord is the Lord of the heavens and the earth, who created them, the One to whom I call you to worship; and I am among those who bear witness to this."

Commentary of the King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 21, verse 57:

﴿And by Allah, I will surely plot against your idols after you have turned away and gone.﴾

Then Ibrahim smashed the idols and reduced them to small pieces, leaving the biggest of them intact, so that the people would return to it and question it, whereby their helplessness and misguidance would become evident, and the proof would be established against them.

The people returned and saw their idols smashed and disgraced, and they asked one another: "Who has done this to our gods? Surely he is a wrongdoer, for his audacity against the gods who deserve to be exalted and revered."
Those who heard Ibrahim swear that he would plot against their idols said: "We heard a young man who speaks ill of the idols, called Ibrahim."

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 21, verse 61:

Their leaders said: "Bring Ibrahim before the eyes of the people, so that they may bear witness to his admission of what he said, and so that this becomes a proof against him."
Abraham was brought forward, and they questioned him, denying the act: "Is it you who broke our gods?" They meant their idols.

Ibrahim had accomplished what he intended: exposing their foolishness before their very eyes. He said, arguing against them and alluding to their stupidity: ﴿Rather, this large idol did it, so ask your supposed gods about it, if they can speak or answer.﴾

Then they were overcome with remorse, and their misguidance became clear to them: how could they worship them, when they are powerless to ward off anything from themselves or to answer one who asks them? And they confessed against themselves to being wrongdoers and polytheists.

Soon after they had been silenced, their obstinacy returned to them. They reverted to falsehood and argued against Ibrahim (Abraham) with what was in fact a proof for him against them, saying: "How can we ask them, when you know that they cannot speak?"

Ibrahim said, belittling the idols: "How can you worship idols that benefit no one if they are worshipped, and do no harm if they are abandoned? Shame on you and on the gods you worship besides Allah, the Exalted. Will you not use your reason, so that you perceive how wrong is the state you are in?"

Ibrahim said, belittling the idols: "How can you worship idols that benefit no one if they are worshipped, and do no harm if they are abandoned? Shame on you and on the gods you worship besides Allah, the Exalted. Will you not use your reason, so that you perceive how wrong is the state you are in?"

When their argument was refuted and the truth became manifest, they resorted to the use of their authority, and said: "Burn Ibrahim (Abraham) with fire, in defense of your gods, if you are going to be helpers of them." So they kindled a great fire and cast him into it. But Allah gave victory to His messenger, and said to the fire: "Be coolness and safety upon Ibrahim." It did him no harm, and no injury befell him.

The people intended to destroy Abraham, but God nullified their scheme and made them the defeated, the lowest.

And We saved Abraham and Lot, who believed in him, from [the land of] "Iraq," and brought them out to the land of "Shām" (Greater Syria), which We blessed with abundant good, and in which most of the prophets, peace be upon them, were sent.

And We bestowed Our favour upon Abraham, granting him Isaac when he called upon Us, and to him We gave Jacob as an addition beyond that. And each of Abraham, Isaac and Jacob, God made them righteous and obedient to Him.

We made Ibrahim, Ishaq and Ya'qub leaders (qudwa) for the people, calling them to the worship of Allah and to obeying Him by His permission, and We revealed to them the doing of good deeds, by acting according to the laws of the prophets, and the establishing of prayer in its proper form, and the giving of zakah. So they complied with that, and they were submissive and obedient to Allah alone, with none besides Him.

And We gave Lut (Lot) prophethood, and judgment between disputants, and knowledge of the command of Allah and His religion, and We rescued him from his town, Sodom (Sadum), whose people used to do wicked deeds. Indeed they were people of evil and ugliness because of the wicked and reprehensible acts they committed, going out of obedience to Allah.

This is a commentary passage on Surah al-Anbiya' (21:75), the verse about Prophet Nuh (Noah). Translation:

God completed His favor upon him, admitting him into His mercy by saving him from what befell his people, because he was among those who acted in obedience to God.

And mention, O Messenger, Noah, when he called upon his Lord before you and before Abraham and Lot. So We answered his supplication and saved him and his family who believed in him from the great distress.
And We aided him against the people who denied Our signs, which testify to his truthfulness. Indeed, they were a people of evil, so We drowned them all in the flood.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 21, verse 78:

Mention, O Messenger, Dawud (David), the prophet of Allah, and his son Sulayman (Solomon), when they were judging a case brought before them by two litigants. The sheep of one of them had strayed onto the field of the other, spreading through it by night and destroying the crops. Dawud ruled that the sheep should become the property of the owner of the field in compensation for what they had destroyed, since their value equalled the value of the damage. And We were witness to their judgment, nothing of it escaping Us.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 21, verse 79:

Then We gave Sulayman (Solomon) understanding of the matter, considering the interests of both parties together with justice. He ruled that the owner of the sheep should repair the damaged crops during a period in which the owner of the crops benefits from the produce of the sheep, such as their milk, wool and the like. Then the sheep are to return to their owner and the crops to their owner, because the value of the crops that were destroyed equals the benefit of the sheep. And to both Dawud (David) and Sulayman We gave judgment and knowledge. We subjected the mountains to Dawud, glorifying God along with him when he glorified Him, and likewise the birds glorified Him, and We were doing that.

Almighty God singled out David, peace be upon him, by teaching him the craft of making armour, which he fashioned as interlinked rings that ease the movement of the body, so as to protect warriors from the impact of weapons upon them. So will you, then, be thankful for God's blessing upon you, in that He brought it about through the hand of His servant David?

And We subjected to Solomon the wind, strong in its blowing, carrying him and those with him; it ran by his command toward the land of Jerusalem (Bayt al-Maqdis) in al-Sham (Greater Syria), which We had blessed with abundant good. And We have knowledge of all things.

And We subjected to Solomon the devils (shayatin), devils who served him in what others could not do. They would dive into the sea for him, bringing forth pearls and jewels, and they would also work at crafts of whatever he desired from them, unable to refuse what he wanted from them. Allah protected them for him by His power and might, glory be to Him and exalted.

Mention, O Messenger, Our servant Ayyub (Job), when We tested him with harm and severe illness in his body, and the loss of his family, his wealth and his children. He was patient and sought reward from Allah, and he called out to his Lord, Mighty and Majestic, saying: "Indeed, harm has touched me, and You are the Most Merciful of the merciful; so relieve me of it."

So We answered his prayer, removed the affliction from him, and restored to him what he had lost of family, children and wealth, doubled. We did this as a mercy from Us, and as a lesson for everyone who endures affliction, hopes for the mercy of his Lord, and worships Him.

And mention Ismail, Idris and Dhul-Kifl. All of them were among those who were patient in obedience to Allah the Most High, patient in refraining from His prohibitions, and patient in the face of His decrees, so they deserved to be remembered with fine praise.
And We admitted them into Our mercy. Indeed, they were among the righteous, whose inner and outer selves were good, who obeyed Allah and acted upon what He commanded them.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 21, verse 87:

Recall the story of the companion of the fish (ṣāḥib al-ḥūt), who was Yunus ibn Matta (ʿalayhi al-salām). Allah sent him to his people, and he called them, but they did not believe. He threatened them with punishment, but they did not turn back in repentance. He did not show patience with them as Allah had commanded him, and he left from among them in anger toward them, his chest constricted by their disobedience. He thought that Allah would not restrict him or hold him accountable for this act of disobedience. So Allah tested him with severe distress and confinement, and the fish swallowed him in the sea. He called out to his Lord in the darknesses of the night, the sea, and the belly of the fish, repentant and acknowledging his wrongdoing for having abandoned patience with his people, saying: ﴿There is no deity except You; glory be to You. Indeed, I have been among the wrongdoers.﴾

**Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 21, verse 88:**

So We answered his prayer and delivered him from the distress of this hardship. And thus do We save those who believe and affirm, and who act in accordance with Our law.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 21, verse 89:

And mention, O Messenger, the story of Zakariyya, the servant of God, when he called upon his Lord to grant him offspring, after he had grown old, saying: "My Lord, do not leave me alone without an heir. Grant me a successor who will uphold the religion among the people after me, and You are the best of those who remain and the best of those who inherit."

So We answered his supplication and granted him Yahya, and We made his wife fit to bear children, having been barren before. Indeed they used to hasten to every good deed, calling upon Us with hope in what is with Us and fear of Our punishment, and they were humbly submissive to Us.

Mention, O Messenger, the story of Maryam (Mary), daughter of Imran, who guarded her chastity from what is unlawful and never committed an immoral act in her life. Then Allah sent Jibril (Gabriel), peace be upon him, to her, and he breathed into the opening of her garment, and the breath reached her womb. By that breath Allah created the Messiah, Isa (Jesus), peace be upon him. She conceived him without a husband, and so she and her son became a sign of Allah's power and a lesson for mankind until the Hour is established.

These prophets, all of them, have one religion, Islam, which is submission to Allah through obedience and devoting worship to Him alone. Allah, glorified and exalted is He, is the Lord of creation, so worship Him alone, O people, with no partner.

But people differed over their messengers, and many of their followers split up in the religion into sects and factions. They worshipped created beings and their own desires, and they will all return to Us and be held accountable for what they did.

Whoever holds fast to faith in Allah and His messengers, and does whatever righteous deeds he is able to do, out of obedience to Allah and worship of Him, then Allah will not waste his deed or nullify it; rather, He will multiply all of it many times over, and he will find what he did recorded in his book on the Day he is raised after his death.

It is impossible for the people of the towns that We destroyed, because of their disbelief and wrongdoing, to return to this world before the Day of Resurrection, so that they might make up for what they neglected.

When the wall of Gog and Magog is opened, and they rush forth from the high ground of the earth and spread out across its expanses, swiftly, the Day of Resurrection draws near and its terrors appear. Then the eyes of the disbelievers will be fixed open from the intensity of their dread, hardly blinking. In anguish they will call down woe upon themselves, saying: "Woe to us! We were truly heedless, unmindful of this Day and of preparing for it, and we were wrongdoers in that."

You (disbelievers) and what you used to worship besides Allah, of idols and of those who were content that you worship them, among jinn and humankind, are fuel for Hell and its firewood. You and they will be entering it.

Had these you worshipped besides God been gods deserving worship, they would not have entered the Fire of Hell along with you, O polytheists. Indeed, each of the worshippers and the worshipped will abide forever in the Fire of Hell.

For those tormented in the Fire there are agonies, of which their groaning is an indication, the groaning in which their breaths are forcefully expelled from their chests; and while in the Fire they do not hear, because of the terror of their torment.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 21, verse 101:

Indeed, those for whom the good reward was already decreed from Us, by Our knowledge that they are among the people of Paradise, those will be kept far away from the Fire. So they will not enter it, and they will not even be near it.

They will not hear the sound of its blaze nor the burning of bodies within it, for they will have settled in their dwellings in Paradise, abiding forever in what their souls desire of its bliss and pleasures.

The Noble Qur'an's commentary (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar), on surah 21, verses 103–104:

The great terror will not grieve them on the Day of Resurrection; rather, the angels will give them good tidings: "This is your Day, which you were promised." Honor from Allah and abundant reward are promised to you in it. On the day when We fold up the heavens as a scroll is folded over what has been written in it, and We will bring forth creation in the same form as Our first creating of them, just as their mothers bore them, that is the promise of Allah which will not be broken. We have made this promise as a true promise binding upon Ourselves; indeed, We are ever the ones who carry out what We promise.

We have certainly written in the revealed Scriptures, after what was written in the Preserved Tablet, that the earth will be inherited by the righteous servants of Allah, who carry out what they were commanded and avoid what they were forbidden. They are the Ummah of Muhammad (ﷺ).

**Commentary of the King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on Surah 21, verse 106:**

Indeed, in this recited (Qur'an) there is sufficient admonition for a people who worship Allah in the way He has prescribed for them and approved of from them.
And We have not sent you, O Messenger, except as a mercy to all people. Whoever believes in you will be happy and saved, and whoever does not believe will be lost and will suffer loss.
Say: What has been revealed to me and what I have been sent with is that your God, the only one who deserves to be worshipped, is Allah. So submit to Him and yield to His worship.

If they turn away from Islam, then say to them: I have conveyed to you all that Allah, exalted is He, has revealed to me; I and you are equal in knowledge of what I have warned and cautioned you about, and I do not know, after that, when the punishment you have been promised will befall you.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 21, verse 110:

Indeed, Allah knows what you utter aloud of your words, and what you conceal in your inner selves, and He will call you to account for it.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 21, verse 111:

"And I do not know; perhaps the delay of the punishment that you have been hastening is a means of drawing you on gradually (istidraj) and a test for you, and that you may enjoy worldly life for a time, so that you may increase in disbelief, and then it will be greater for your punishment."

The Prophet ﷺ said: "My Lord, judge between us and our people who deny the true judgment." And we ask our Lord, the Most Merciful, and seek His help against what you (O disbelievers) describe, of associating partners with Him, denying Him, and fabricating lies against Him, and against what you threaten us with of triumph and victory over us.
